raw_text: Publish a fixed candidate when ready for independent review. Please include which files you changed and a short reproduction of the expected behavior (ConciseDateFormatter should show the year in the offset string when the plotted span is <1 year and January is not included, e.g. Feb 2021 - Aug 2021 -> offsettext "2021"). I will adopt the exact patch, run public tests on that same version, then accept or request changes.

Final candidate patch-1 is published (source version v2). Please adopt it, run public tests on that exact version, then accept or request changes.

Changed file: lib/matplotlib/dates.py only (ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks).

What changed: the level-detection loop previously did `if level < 2: show_offset = False`, which suppressed the offset for day/hour/minute/second-level ticks. Now, after the level is found:
- if level < 2 and no tick is in January (np.any(tickdate[:, 1] == 1) is False): keep show_offset True and set level = 1, so the offset uses offset_formats[1] = '%Y' -> offset text "2021";
- if level < 2 and a January tick exists: show_offset = False (unchanged; the year already appears in that tick's label).

Reproduction (issue snippet, Feb 2021 - Aug 2021):
  import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, matplotlib.dates as mdates
  from datetime import datetime, timedelta
  initial = datetime(2021, 2, 14)
  time_array = [initial + timedelta(days=x) for x in range(1, 200)]
  data = [-x**2/20000 for x in range(1, 200)]
  fig, ax = plt.subplots()
  ax.plot(time_array, data)
  locator = mdates.AutoDateLocator(); formatter = mdates.ConciseDateFormatter(locator)
  ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(locator); ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
  fig.canvas.draw()
  ax.xaxis.get_offset_text().get_text()  # expected '2021' (was '' before the fix)

My own public test evidence on this version: pytest lib/matplotlib/tests/test_dates.py -> 89 collected / 89 passed / 0 failed (includes test_concise_formatter, test_concise_formatter_show_offset, test_offset_changes, test_concise_formatter_tz and the usetex variants). Please verify independently rather than relying on my report.

INDEPENDENT REVIEW RESULT: ACCEPT (review-1) for patch-1.

Evidence I produced myself on the adopted candidate:
- Adopted patch-1 into my private tree; my resulting tree files_sha256 = 6cc2c81ed37bb9bbdcb46b31e3eb64e307357e381653f66dd7a314163a534224, identical to patch-1's files_sha256, so my test run was on your exact candidate content.
- I removed my own scratch probe test files before the final run so nothing of mine was mixed in.
- Fresh same-version public execution: lib/matplotlib/tests/test_dates.py => 89 collected, 89 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (report test-report-315b77e235cd9447cc0f98a8, sequence 43).
- Issue reproduction: datetime(2021,2,14) + 200 days with AutoDateLocator + ConciseDateFormatter now yields offset string '2021', which is exactly the expected outcome in the issue ("I expect the year 2021 to show in the offset").
- I initially suspected the `level = 1` assignment was an unintended side effect changing tick labels. On inspection it is correct and necessary: level=1 is what selects offsetfmts[1] = '%Y', and the resulting month-name labels for sub-year spans are consistent with the existing public expectations in test_concise_formatter / test_concise_formatter_show_offset, all of which pass.

Notes for delivery: patch-1 touches only lib/matplotlib/dates.py (ConciseDateFormatter.format_ticks), which is appropriately minimal. Acceptance is not integration and not official scoring — you still own the final step: integrate patch-1 into your tree (or keep it as your endpoint), run the public tests on that exact final version, fix_patch(task_ids=[]), then submit_integration. If you change anything in dates.py from now on, that is new content and needs a fresh candidate and a fresh review from me.
